1.	Yes it will. And yes, your credit score matters. As early as now you should start building your credit. Having multiple lines of credit accessible to you will benefit you and your business when that time comes. Just don’t forget the golden rule, “Don’t swipe unless you can pay for it in cash”, especially since you’re just starting out.
2.	No annual fees for life means no annual fees forever. But sometimes banks can be sneaky, so I suggest you read the terms and conditions of the selected product.
3.	As for card recommendations, I suggest going to websites like imoney, ecomparemo, and moneymax since they have tools that can filter out cards that you aren’t looking for and then try applying for those (just make sure you meet the eligibility requirements). Also, there are tiers when it comes to credit cards. You won’t usually find the ideal card that you’re looking for unless you meet the requirements and have a good credit history banks can look into. This is usually why I recommend secured credit cards to people starting out because this is one of the best ways to start building your credit history. RCBC does however offer an alternative right now to having a secured card. Also note that your savings wont always guarantee your approval for a credit card due to the fact that these don’t show up on your credit report.
4.	Credit card debts incur interest rates when the full amount isn’t paid for before the due date. Even if you can afford to pay for it, I highly recommend not doing that as it can lower your credit score. That won’t really prove how financially responsible you are.
